info.title: Terrain Viewer tile service
info.description: What Terrain Viewer draws, as map tiles and as pictures of a viewport. Two engines draw them. The direct engine computes every 2D terrain mode in the server with the app's own code, reading the elevation with the app's own readers (tile pyramids, COG, VRT, WMS and WCS, LERC, quantized mesh, PMTiles, differences), in a fraction of a second. For everything else the app itself renders them in a headless browser, so every source it reads and every mode it computes comes out as in the app: a tile is drawn with the 2048 px block around it and the block is kept a week, so the first tile of a block takes seconds and its neighbours milliseconds. Web Mercator only.

get.description: A 256 px Web Mercator tile. For 512 px write `{y}@2x` in the address or add `tilesize=512`. The camera is the tile's: `lat`, `lng`, `zoom`, `pitch` and `bearing` are not read.

parameters.name: tilesize
parameters.description: The side of the tile in pixels.

parameters.name: terrainSource
parameters.description: The elevation source: an id from `/sources`, the address of Terrarium tiles, of a COG (`.tif`) or of a VRT (`.vrt`), or a configuration as JSON with the fields of a library entry, `{"url": ..., "type": "terrarium" | "terrainrgb" | "cog" | "vrt" | "wms-raw" | "lerc" | "quantized-mesh" | "tilejson", "maxzoom": ...}`. Unset: Mapterhorn. `url` is read as the same parameter.

parameters.name: engine
parameters.description: Who draws. `direct`: computed in the server from elevation tiles, in a fraction of a second, for the modes and parameters `/algorithms` lists as direct on a source `/sources` lists as direct. `browser`: the app in a headless browser, every source and mode, seconds. `auto` (the default) takes direct when it can. The answer's `x-tv-engine` header says which drew it, `x-tv-engine-why` why not direct.

parameters.name: background
parameters.description: `none`: no white (or black) map background, a transparent PNG to stack layers in a GIS. Direct engine only; the browser's tiles keep the map's background.

parameters.name: modes
parameters.description: The modes to draw, comma-separated. Unset: hillshade. Given without `hillshade`, the hillshade is off. `algorithm` is read as the same parameter.

parameters.name: mapboxKey
parameters.description: Your Mapbox access token, for the `mapbox` source. Read by the server's readers and given to the app as a setting, never put in the app's address; a tile drawn with a key is cached apart from one without.

parameters.name: maptilerKey
parameters.description: Your MapTiler key, for the `maptiler` source.

parameters.name: cesiumIonKey
parameters.description: Your Cesium ion token, for the `cesium` source and other ion assets.

parameters.name: imageryUrl
parameters.description: Imagery under the terrain: XYZ tiles (`{z}/{x}/{y}`) or a COG. Shown with the mode `basemap`.

parameters.name: imagerySource
parameters.description: Dated imagery built into the app, with `imageryDate`.

parameters.name: imageryDate
parameters.description: The date of `imagerySource`, YYYY-MM-DD.

parameters.name: appParams
parameters.description: Any other URL parameter of the app, given as it is at the top level of the query (for example `slopeOpacity=0.6`): ramps, opacities, light direction, contour interval. The list is the app's URL reference.

400.description: A parameter is wrong; the body says which

500.description: The app could not be rendered; the body says why

get.description: Like a WMS GetMap: a picture of a given size, placed by its centre and zoom or by a bounding box. Unlike a tile it keeps the scale bar and the credits, and it can be tilted or split.

parameters.name: lat
parameters.description: Latitude of the centre. Required unless `bbox` is given.

parameters.name: lng
parameters.description: Longitude of the centre. Required unless `bbox` is given.

parameters.name: zoom
parameters.description: MapLibre zoom (512 px tiles).

parameters.name: bbox
parameters.description: west,south,east,north in degrees, in place of `lat`, `lng` and `zoom`. The whole box is inside the picture; when its shape differs from the picture's, more is shown on two sides.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Width in pixels.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Height in pixels.

parameters.name: viewMode
parameters.description: Flat, tilted over the relief, or the globe.

parameters.name: pitch
parameters.description: Tilt in degrees; 55 by default in 3D.

parameters.name: bearing
parameters.description: Rotation in degrees, clockwise from north.

parameters.name: split
parameters.description: Two views in one picture, with `terrainSourceB`.

parameters.name: terrainSourceB
parameters.description: The second view's elevation source.

get.description: The tile address for the given parameters, as a TileJSON document a map library can load. `tile_format` (png, jpg; pbf or mvt for the vector tiles, then TileJSON 3.0 with the `vector_layers` of the modes) and `tile_scale` (1, 2) choose the tiles; every other parameter is kept in the tile address. `/tilejson.json` is the same.

get.description: Every elevation source the app knows: the built-in ones and the library. Each with its type, its tile address when it is a plain pyramid, its zoom range and extent, and the engine that can draw it.
The app's ramps, to name as `colorRamp` (colour relief) or `slopeColorRamp` (slope).
Its stops, as a MapLibre expression over the value.

get.summary: The overlays as a vector tile
get.description: The tile address with `.pbf` or `.mvt`: a Mapbox Vector Tile (512 px tiles, as the map loads them) with the features the app's overlays draw, one layer each: `contours` (lines with `ele` and `level`), the iso-line (`isoband` polygons and `isoline` lines at a value, `isoline-cliff` the cliff edge on a slope; `isoline` lines every interval), the mound detector (`tells` points with their measures) and the graticule (`graticule` lines, `kind` meridian or parallel, `deg`). Same parameters as the raster tiles; `/tiles/WebMercatorQuad/...` is the same. Past a layer's last zoom it comes from its deepest tile, scaled up. A mode drawn only as an image (hillshade, the plane slicer, ...) is refused: ask for `.png` or `.jpg`.

parameters.name: terrainSource
parameters.description: The elevation source: an id from `/sources`, a tile address or a JSON configuration.

parameters.name: modes
parameters.description: The layers, comma-separated. Unset: contours.

parameters.name: appParams
parameters.description: The app's parameters of these layers, as for the raster tiles (contourMinor, isolineValue, tellSize, graticuleDensity, ...).

400.description: A mode is not served as vector tiles, or the source cannot be read by the direct engine

get.summary: A QGIS project of a view
get.description: Every layer of the app as an XYZ layer (transparent tiles, `background=none`), stacked as the map stacks them and grouped as its panel where that order allows: the overlays on top (contours, plane slicer, mound candidates, graticule, iso-line, each also as vector tiles), the lighting effects, the hillshade, relief visualization, terrain analysis, the colour relief, then the basemap (as the app draws it, with its overlays; a plain XYZ basemap as such too; Google hybrid). The layers the view switches on start checked, and every layer's address carries the view's settings. The query is the view, in the service's names (terrainSource, modes, imageryUrl...) or the app's own: the query of a share link works as is (terrainSourceA, show* switches, ramps, basemapSource, overlayBasemapIds...). lat, lng and zoom set the project's extent. Without a query: every layer unchecked but the Google hybrid basemap.

parameters.name: terrainSource
parameters.description: The elevation source of every layer (or terrainSourceA, the app's name).

parameters.name: modes
parameters.description: The layers to check, comma-separated; or the app's show* parameters.

parameters.name: appParams
parameters.description: Any of the app's URL parameters, kept in every layer's address.

get.summary: The modes, and which engine draws them
The modes with their settings, grouped as the app's panel
get.description: What the QGIS plugin builds its panel from: the app's panel groups, top drawn on top; for each mode its form (`raster`, `vector` or `both`), whether it is shading (opaque tiles, multiplied over the layers under it), the parameter of its opacity and its settings (the app's URL parameters, with type, allowed values and default). Given a view's query (a share link's, as is), `view` lists the modes it switches on, their opacities, the parameters every layer keeps and the camera.

parameters.name: appParams
parameters.description: A view: the query of a share link, as is.
